title: Final Project Plan: NCAA Women’s Volleyball Statistics
text:
Key Variables of Interest
The dataset contains thousands of observations detailing team performance and play-by-play actions sourced from Matt Waite’s repository and public data. The primary variables I plan to explore include:

Kills & Errors: Measuring offensive efficiency and unforced mistakes.
Total Attacks & Hitting Percentage: Evaluating overall offensive production.
Serve Receive & Digs: Analyzing defensive stability under pressure.
Blocks (Solo/Assists): Gauging net defense effectiveness.

title: Final Project Plan: NCAA Women’s Volleyball Statistics
text:
Exploratory Data Visualization
Below is an exploratory graphic examining the relationship between kills and errors across NCAA divisions:

library(ggplot2)

# Sample exploratory data
set.seed(42)
n <- 120
vb_data <- data.frame(
  kills = c(rnorm(n/2, mean = 25, sd = 5), rnorm(n/2, mean = 12, sd = 3)),
  errors = c(rnorm(n/2, mean = 15, sd = 4), rnorm(n/2, mean = 6, sd = 2)),
  division = rep(c("Division I", "Division II"), each = n/2)
)

ggplot(vb_data, aes(x = errors, y = kills, color = division)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "NCAA Volleyball Performance",
    x = "Errors",
    y = "Kills",
    color = "Division"
  )







Figure 1: NCAA Volleyball: Kills vs. Errors by Division
